key_insight: A Petri-net execution harness can block unsafe agent tool calls, but allowing every safe action need not minimize costly replanning.
engineering_relevance: Encoding capabilities, approvals, and budgets as execution preconditions makes tool-call authorization independent of injected wording.
method: Model tool execution as Petri-net supervisory control, treating tool outcomes as uncontrollable.
Analyze a replanning closed loop where each retry incurs an inference call.
Refine the conventional safe supervisor using value thresholds to minimize intrusiveness for a given proposer model.
evidence_signal: Formal analysis shows the conventional supervisor can be arbitrarily more intrusive than a stricter safe supervisor; synthesis on an autonomous release agent identifies a necessary refusal-capable step after rollout begins.
watch_item: Safety transfer to the running system depends on four assumptions, while least-intrusive control depends on the chosen proposer model.
paper_title: Certified Execution Harness for Agentic AI: Safe and Least-Intrusive Petri-Net Supervisory Control Between Reasoning and Action
